_meta.description: Human-annotated ground truth for ShieldScan AI triage evaluation

labels.TRUE_POSITIVE: Finding is a real vulnerability that must be fixed
labels.FALSE_POSITIVE: Finding is not exploitable in context — scanner over-fired

findings.notes: Direct string concatenation of userId into SELECT — classic SQL injection sink
Template literal interpolation of name into SQL string — user-controlled input reaches query
req.query passed directly to MongoDB find() — allows operator injection e.g. {$gt:''}
req.body passed directly to findOne() — auth bypass via {$ne:null} is trivial
Unsanitized userInput assigned to innerHTML — classic stored/reflected XSS sink
req.params.filename used directly in fs.readFile — ../../etc/passwd traversal possible
Scanner fired on the comment line containing 'eval()' — not executable code
eval(expression) with externally supplied expression — arbitrary code execution
Scanner matched 'child_process.*exec' against a comment line — not executable code
jwt.decode() does not verify the signature — attacker can forge any token payload
jwt.verify(token, null) disables signature verification — equivalent to jwt.decode()
MD5 used to hash passwords — broken for this use case, rainbow tables exist
Scanner fired on a comment line mentioning 'token' and 'Math.random()' — not code
Math.random() used as session token — predictable, not cryptographically secure
Object.assign onto existing object with req.body — __proto__ key injection possible
cors({ origin: '*' }) allows any domain to make cross-origin requests with credentials
Hardcoded demo API key in source — still a real secret-management finding because credentials are embedded in code and git history
user.password logged to console — appears in log aggregation systems (CloudWatch, Splunk)
innerHTML receives output of escapeHtml() — sanitized before assignment, not exploitable
SHA-1 used for content-addressed cache key, not for auth/signing — collision attacks do not apply here
Scanner fired on a comment line that mentions 'key' and 'Math.random()' — not code
cacheKey matched 'key' substring — this is a transient UI deduplication id, not a cryptographic secret
Scanner fired on comment text '127.0.0.1 is localhost' — not a hardcoded production endpoint
127.0.0.1 is the loopback address — not a production secret; used only in local dev config
Value 'Change_Me_On_First_Login!' is an explicit placeholder — not a real credential
